_meta.how_to_regress: npm run check:golden drive-home  (dev backend up)
_meta.note: V2 rewrite, 2026-08-25. Replaces the v1 sample outright: the old tool ran web_search and spoke confidently about named highways and interchanges it could not see. safety_overview, risk_level, honest_assessment, checklist and before_you_go are gone, and there is no risk score of any kind. The endpoint takes enum ids (time_of_day, road_type, driver_state, conditions[]), not display labels. limits is ONE server-written string. SECTION RULES, clamped in finalise(): watch_for and prep_checklist are GO-only; safer_options is for pause and do_not_drive only; factors_in_favor is usually [] on anything but a go, because an observation about the driver is not a thing that makes the driving safer. Case 1 is the only case here with a non-empty favor/watch/prep, and that is the point — compare the four against it. driver_state "very_tired" is a SERVER-SIDE boundary: case 4 returns do_not_drive from a localized string table without calling the model, so it must stay byte-stable and must never contain English. Case 3 is the German stress case (four conditions plus a long concern) and guards against truncation. Case 2 is the tool at its best: before_you_decide naming an official road-conditions source and what a closure or a restriction would mean. Case 5 is the grounding case — this exact input produced "Heavy traffic — evening commute conditions", "low-visibility weather", a 20-30 minute recovery prescription, and safer_options inventing a colleague and someone at home. OUTPUT DISCIPLINE and STATE-SPECIFIC OUTPUT RULES were added 2026-08-25 and the sanitiser caps were aligned to them: harder 5, favor 4, safer 4, prep 3, watch 2. A GO answer is now materially SHORTER than a pause — case 1 is ~850 chars against ~1800-2000 for cases 2, 3 and 5. If a future capture shows GO growing back toward the others, the discipline block has stopped working. READ cases 2 and 5 after any prompt change; structure alone will not catch a regression in either. optionalSections on a case names the arrays this tool is DESIGNED to leave empty, so a run that correctly returns [] is not read as a regression; safer_options on a pause and factors_harder on a pause are NOT optional and stay asserted.

input.concern: It is much later than I meant to stay out.

output.headline: Nothing in what you've reported gives a clear reason to wait.
output.summary: You report feeling fine, conditions are clear, and the drive is a short city-street trip. Staying later than planned isn't itself a driving concern, though late-night driving on city streets does carry its own considerations.
factors_harder: Late-night city driving means visibility depends entirely on street lighting and your headlights; if either is poor on your route, that matters.
prep_checklist: Before you start, check whether drowsiness or fogginess has appeared since you decided to drive.
limits: Drive Home doesn't have live traffic, weather, or road-condition data. This assessment uses only what you reported. If conditions change, reassess before leaving.

input.concern: I have not driven in snow since last winter and I do not know how the pass looks.

output.headline: Check current road and pass conditions before committing to this drive.
output.summary: You have reported snow or ice, high wind, and highway driving at roughly 90 minutes. You have also flagged a specific unknown — the condition of the pass — and limited recent snow-driving experience. That unknown is concrete and checkable, and it materially affects whether this drive is reasonable to start.
output.main_concern: The pass condition is unverified. Snow or ice combined with high wind on a highway can vary dramatically over short distances, and you have identified this directly as your hesitation.
factors_harder: Reported snow or ice on a highway route
Reported high wind, which can reduce visibility and vehicle stability independently of road surface
Self-reported gap in recent snow-driving experience
Pass condition is currently unknown to you
output.before_you_decide: Check the current road condition report for the pass before deciding. Look for a state department of transportation road-conditions site or traveler information line — these typically report surface conditions, chain or traction laws, and whether a road is closed or restricted. If the pass is closed, under a restriction you are not equipped for, or rated at a severity beyond your current comfort level, do not start. If conditions are reported as manageable and you feel ready, you can proceed wit
safer_options: Wait somewhere safe, recheck the pass and weather conditions, and reassess before starting.
If a driver with recent winter highway experience is available, that person could make the drive instead.
Delay the trip until a forecast window with reduced wind and precipitation, if that is an option
If the pass is closed or restricted, consider whether the trip can be postponed entirely
limits: Drive Home doesn't have live traffic, weather, or road-condition data. This assessment uses only what you reported. If conditions change, reassess before leaving.

input.concern: Die Sicht wird schlechter und ich kenne die Umleitung durch die Baustelle nicht.

output.headline: Kurze Pause empfohlen – eine konkrete Unklarheit lässt sich vor der Abfahrt klären.
output.summary: Die Unklarheit über die Umleitung bei gleichzeitig sinkender Sichtweite ist der Punkt, der sich vor der Abfahrt klären lässt. Danach können Sie neu beurteilen, ob die Fahrt passt.
output.main_concern: Unbekannte Umleitung bei aktiv sinkender Sichtweite durch Nebel und Regen – beides zusammen, spät nachts.
factors_harder: Nebel und Regen gleichzeitig – Sichtweite sinkt nach eigenen Angaben weiter
Starker Verkehr spät in der Nacht erhöht Überraschungspotenzial
75 Minuten Fahrtzeit bei diesen Bedingungen ohne Ortskenntnis der Umleitung
factors_in_favor: Fahrer fühlt sich nach eigenen Angaben fit
output.before_you_decide: Klären Sie vor der Abfahrt, wie die Umleitung verläuft – zum Beispiel über eine aktuelle Navigationsapp, die Baustellenbeschilderung vorab auf einer Karte nachvollziehen oder eine offizielle Verkehrsinformationsquelle (z. B. Verkehrslagebericht des zuständigen Landesbetriebs). Wenn Sie die Umleitung kennen oder eingespeichert haben, entfällt der Hauptgrund für diese Empfehlung.
safer_options: Umleitung jetzt am Rechner oder Gerät einsehen und in ein Navigationsgerät einprogrammieren – erst dann abfahren
Warten, bis der Nebel sich etwas hebt oder der Verkehr nachlässt, dann neu beurteilen
Falls verfügbar, jemanden bitten, die Fahrt zu übernehmen, der die Strecke kennt
Falls möglich, die Nacht am Büro oder in der Nähe verbringen und bei Tageslicht und besserer Sicht fahren
limits: Drive Home hat keine Live-Daten zu Verkehr, Wetter oder Straßenzustand. Diese Einschätzung verwendet nur das, was du angegeben hast. Wenn sich die Bedingungen ändern, bewerte die Fahrt vor der Abfahrt neu.

output.headline: Fahre jetzt nicht los, wenn du sehr müde bist.
output.summary: Die wichtigste Information ist deine aktuelle Müdigkeit. Verschiebe die Fahrt oder nutze eine andere Möglichkeit, nach Hause zu kommen, statt mit starker Müdigkeit zu fahren.
output.main_concern: Du hast angegeben, sehr müde zu sein.
output.before_you_decide: Bewerte die Fahrt erst neu, wenn du wirklich ausgeruht bist und Wachbleiben und Konzentration kein Problem mehr sind.
safer_options: Warte und ruhe dich aus, bevor du die Fahrt neu bewertest.
Bleib dort, wenn das praktikabel ist.
Bitte eine ausgeruhte Person zu fahren.
Nutze Taxi, Fahrdienst, öffentliche Verkehrsmittel oder eine andere verfügbare Alternative.
limits: Drive Home hat keine Live-Daten zu Verkehr, Wetter oder Straßenzustand. Diese Einschätzung verwendet nur das, was du angegeben hast. Wenn sich die Bedingungen ändern, bewerte die Fahrt vor der Abfahrt neu.

input.concern: I caught myself yawning on the walk to the car and it is raining harder than when I arrived.

output.headline: Worth pausing a few minutes before starting — the combination of tiredness and heavier rain is worth taking seriously.
output.summary: You've reported feeling a little tired, caught yourself yawning on the way to the car, and noticed the rain has intensified since you arrived. Any one of those alone might not shift the call, but together — on a 45-minute mixed-road drive in heavy evening traffic — they make a short pause before departure the prudent move.
output.main_concern: Self-reported tiredness combined with yawning and worsening rain heading into a 45-minute drive in heavy traffic.
factors_harder: Yawning before even reaching the car is a concrete signal of fatigue, not just a feeling.
Rain has worsened since you arrived at the office.
Heavy traffic extends the time you need to stay fully attentive.
45 minutes on mixed roads in rain requires sustained focus.
factors_in_favor: You noticed the fatigue and the worsening rain before starting — not mid-drive.
output.before_you_decide: Sit quietly for a few minutes without driving. Notice whether the yawning continues or the tiredness feels worse. If either does, that is a reason to delay further or hand the drive to someone else if that option exists. If you feel more alert after the rest, reassess then.
safer_options: Wait somewhere safe and reassess before starting.
If a rested person is available, ask them to drive instead.
If another mode of transport is available for this route, use it and avoid driving in your current state.
If the option exists, delay until you feel more alert.
limits: Drive Home doesn't have live traffic, weather, or road-condition data. This assessment uses only what you reported. If conditions change, reassess before leaving.
